Electricity: Cold-Store Construction and Refrigeration
A cold store uses electrically powered refrigeration equipment to cool a fully enclosed room and extend the storage life of food inside containers.

Required Components
• Refrigerant piping
• Cold-store insulation
• Cold-store door
• Cold-store air cooler
• Condensing unit

Equipment Placement
The air cooler must be placed inside the cold-store room and supplied with 128V electrical power. It may not replace a wall block. The condensing unit must be outside the room. Connect both machines using continuous refrigerant piping.

Room Requirements
The room must be completely enclosed and may not exceed 14 interior blocks along any axis. It may contain one single door or one correctly linked double-door pair. Use rightmouse to open or close a door. Opening either door immediately disables the cold store.

Insulation Requirements
The cold-store door is the only boundary that does not require cold-store insulation. Every other wall, floor and ceiling surface facing the interior must be covered. Hold the insulation and use rightmouse on the required interior surface. Insulation may be attached independently to all six faces of a block.

Covered Wall Pipes
Refrigerant piping can be covered with a full block in the same way as a wooden axle. Hold the covering block in the main hand, hold a wrench in the off hand, then hold sprint and use rightmouse on the pipe. A covered pipe remains connected and can form part of the sealed room boundary. The face of the covering block facing the cold-store interior must still receive cold-store insulation. The covering block does not replace the insulation layer. An uncovered pipe cannot be used as a cold-store wall.

Temperature and Preservation
At full requested power, the air cooler reduces the cold store from its current temperature to -50°C in 100 seconds. Cooling speed is reduced by 10% for every 1% of missing input power. The air cooler cannot refrigerate the room when supplied power is at or below 90% of the requested power. At -50°C, containers inside the room can reach a 0.025x perish-rate multiplier. Loss of power, an open door, a broken pipe network or an invalid structure causes the room to warm gradually and reduces the preservation effect.
blockdesc-aircooler-*: A 128V refrigeration device installed inside a cold store. Power demand equals 1W for every interior block.
aircooler-cooling-behavior: At full power, the air cooler can reduce the cold store from its current temperature to -50°C in 100 seconds. Cooling speed is reduced by 10% for every 1% of missing input power. The air cooler cannot operate when supplied power is at or below 90% of the requested power.
block-handbooktext-aircooler: The refrigeration terminal installed inside a cold store. It requires electrical power and a refrigerant-pipe connection to a condensing unit outside the room. Read the cold-store construction and refrigeration guide for complete structural requirements.
blockdesc-condensingunit-*: The outdoor part of the refrigeration circuit. It must be connected to the indoor air cooler through continuous refrigerant piping.
block-handbooktext-condensingunit: The outdoor component of the cold-store refrigeration circuit. It must be connected through refrigerant piping to an air cooler inside the cold store. Read the cold-store construction and refrigeration guide for details.
blockdesc-refrigerantpipe: Connects the air cooler and condensing unit. It can be covered with a full block where it passes through a sealed wall.
block-handbooktext-refrigerantpipe: Connects the air cooler to the condensing unit. Refrigerant piping can be covered with a full block where it passes through a sealed room boundary. Read the cold-store construction and refrigeration guide for details.
blockdesc-coldstore-insulation: A metallic insulation layer that can be attached independently to all six faces of a full block.
block-handbooktext-coldstore-insulation: A metallic insulation layer designed for cold stores. Hold the insulation, aim at the face of a full block that faces the cold-store interior, and use rightmouse to place it. Insulation can be attached independently to all six faces of the same block. Except for the cold-store door, every interior wall, floor and ceiling surface must be covered with insulation. If refrigerant piping has been covered with a full block, the face of that covering block facing the cold-store interior must also be insulated. Read the Cold-Store Construction and Refrigeration Guide for details.
blockdesc-coldstoredoor: An airtight metal door for cold-store entrances. It can be used as a single door or a linked double-door pair.
block-handbooktext-coldstoredoor: An airtight metal door used to seal a cold-store entrance. Aim at the door and use rightmouse to open or close it. A cold store may use one single door or one correctly linked pair of adjacent double doors. Opening either door immediately stops refrigeration. The cold-store door is the only cold-store boundary that does not require an additional insulation layer. Read the Cold-Store Construction and Refrigeration Guide for details.
